sections.label: Mobile data usage growth
sections.summary: Total mobile data usage has more than doubled since 2012 due to increased smartphone penetration and data-intensive applications like mobile video streaming.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Total mobile data usage has more than doubled since 2012, due to increased smartphone penetration and the use of data-intensive applications, such as mobile video streaming.

sections.label: Cable-cut offences prosecution approach
sections.summary: The Ministry will not raise the maximum composition amount for compoundable offences under the TA from $5,000 to $10,000, and will instead prosecute and seek harsher sentences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: First, my Ministry has decided not to proceed with increasing the maximum composition amount for compoundable offences under the TA from $5,000 to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Given the seriousness of cable-cut incidents and their adverse impact on end users, we have assessed that a more effective and targeted deterrent approach would be to focus on actively prosecuting and seeking harsher criminal sentences for such offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This effort is underscored by IMDA's recent prosecution of a Page: 19 case which has led to Court fines totalling $165,000 in 2015.

sections.label: Ban on exclusive building arrangements
sections.summary: Clause 11 will prohibit building owners from entering into exclusive arrangements that limit end users' choice of telecoms service provider.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To provide end users with the freedom to access telecom services from the operator of their choice, clause 11 will prohibit building owners from entering into exclusive arrangements that have the effect of limiting end users' choice of telecoms service provider.

sections.label: Mandatory ADR scheme participation
sections.summary: Participation in the ADR scheme will be mandatory for service providers, while consumers may resolve disputes through the ADR scheme or other avenues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As such, participation in the ADR scheme will be made mandatory for service providers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Consumers, however, will have the flexibility to resolve their disputes through the ADR scheme, or through other avenues, such as the Courts or Small Claims Tribunal.

sections.label: IMDA codes on personal data
sections.summary: Clause 12 amends section 26(1) to let IMDA issue or approve codes or standards authorising collection, use or disclosure of personal data without end users' consent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Clause 12 amends section 26(1) to allow IMDA to issue or approve codes of practice or standards of performance authorising the collection, use or disclosure of personal data by telecoms licensees without end users' consent.

sections.label: IMDA merger condition directions
sections.summary: Clause 15 inserts a new section 32DA to empower IMDA to issue directions to enforce conditions of approval for mergers and acquisitions involving designated entities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Clause 15 inserts a new section 32DA to empower IMDA to issue directions to enforce conditions of approval for mergers and acquisitions involving a designated telecoms licensee, business trust or designated trust.

sections.label: Cap on mobile operators
sections.summary: The question asks whether IMDA would cap the total number of mobile operators deploying equipment on the same building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given the possibility of a fourth mobile operator entering the market, I would like to know if IMDA would be imposing a cap on the total number of mobile operators that can deploy their telecommunications equipment on the same building.

sections.label: Rent-free space for deployments
sections.summary: The question asks whether rent-free space IMDA allocates under COPIF for telecommunications deployments in buildings would be increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In addition, will the amount of rent-free space that IMDA currently allocates under its Code of Practice for Info-communication Facilities in Buildings (COPIF) for telecommunications deployments in buildings be increased to account for this proposal?

sections.label: ADR services payment and binding
sections.summary: The question asks whether consumers must pay for ADR services and whether the ADR outcome is legally binding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will consumers have to pay for ADR services and will the outcome of the ADR process be legally binding?

sections.label: THAAD protestors and IMDA powers
sections.summary: Protestors complained authorities withheld information on electro-magnetic wave risks, and section 32D lets IMDA override certain Acts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But the protestors' complaint was largely that the authorities were not forthcoming with any information on the potential risks, in terms of electro-magnetic waves, on the hundreds of villagers who live and farm in the region where the THAAD system would be deployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There is section 32D where the IMDA has the power to issue their actions, "override the provisions of the Business Trusts Act, Companies Act, Limited Liability Partnerships Act, Trustees Act and the Futures Act".

sections.label: Preventing disruption and section 14 amendments
sections.summary: The question asks how disruption of telecommunications would be prevented, and the amendments add steps for resolving objections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, in terms of safety of equipment and the potential for deliberate acts to disrupt telecommunications in Singapore, could the Minister Page: 23 comment on how this would be prevented, going forward?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These amendments include operational improvements and also provide clarity on how telecommunications operators are regulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments also lay an important foundation for the introduction of next generation mobile technology, which includes the building up of our Smart Nation sensor network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments to section 14 add an additional step where the "Authority must notify the public telecommunications licensee concerned to resolve the dispute with the objector due to the objection".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Also, "on receipt of the Authority's notice, the public telecommunications licensee must take genuine steps to resolve the dispute with the objector due to the objection".

sections.label: Small Claims Tribunal mediation benchmark
sections.summary: The benchmark to beat is the Small Claims Tribunal, where mediation services cost $10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The benchmark to beat is the Small Claims Tribunal where mediation services cost $10.

sections.label: ADR improvement and consumer charges
sections.summary: The passage asks how the ADR will improve on the current situation and how much it will charge consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How will the ADR improve on this and how much will the ADR charge consumers for this service?

sections.label: Telcos pay deployment costs
sections.summary: The amendments require telcos to pay appropriate costs of deployment, such as increasing load-bearing capacity or improving aesthetics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The amendments require telcos to pay "appropriate costs of deployment", such as increasing load-bearing capacity or improving aesthetics.

sections.label: IMDA balancing national interests and investments
sections.summary: The passage asks how IMDA intends to balance protecting national interests with extracting benefits from cross-border investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How does IMDA intend to balance these two contradictory tensions – the need to protect national interests, while also extracting the benefits that cross-border investments could bring?

sections.label: ADR, rooftop space, oversight framework
sections.summary: The ADR, rooftop space clarification and stronger oversight are steps to create a more robust telecommunications framework for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The introduction of an ADR, clarification of rooftop space usage and strengthening of the oversight mechanism are important steps to create a more robust framework for the telecommunications sector in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This Bill will help to advance Singapore's position as a Smart Nation and leading telecommunications hub in the world.

sections.label: IMDA public consultation on scheme design
sections.summary: IMDA will hold a public consultation on the scheme's operational design once the empowering legislative framework is in place.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As mentioned in my opening speech, IMDA will hold a public consultation exercise on the operational design of the scheme once the empowering legislative framework is in place.

sections.label: ADR funding and subscriber fees
sections.summary: IMDA's current thinking is that licensees will provide most ADR funding, with subscribers paying a nominal fee to dissuade frivolous claims.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In relation to the concerns over funding and charges for the ADR scheme, IMDA's current thinking is that the licensees will provide the bulk of the funding.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: A nominal fee will also be paid by subscribers because we want to dissuade frivolous claims.

sections.label: Rooftop space for mobile equipment
sections.summary: Proposed amendments envisage building owners must provide rooftop space as MDS if mobile operators request it, with possible costs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: And these costs may include security escorts to rooftop access, increasing load bearing capacity of the building and the utility bills for running mobile equipment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, with the proposed amendments, it is envisaged that building owners must provide rooftop space as MDS if the mobile operators request it.

sections.label: IMDA annual objections from building owners
sections.summary: IMDA receives about 30 objections every year from building owners or occupiers involved in this process.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: On average, Madam, IMDA receives about 30 such objections every year from building owners or occupiers involved in this process.

sections.label: IMDA inquiry after unresolved dispute
sections.summary: If a dispute remains unresolved, the telecommunications licensee informs IMDA, which typically holds an inquiry within 14 days.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Thereafter, if the dispute remains unresolved, the telecommunications licensee will inform IMDA and IMDA will typically hold an inquiry within the next 14 days.

sections.label: Liberalised telecom market and section 32(d)
sections.summary: Singapore's liberalised telecom market has no foreign ownership restrictions, and amendments will specify laws overridden by section 32(d) directions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: First, I would like to take this opportunity to clarify that Singapore has a liberalised telecommunications market whereby IMDA does not impose restrictions on foreign ownership and control in telecommunications licensees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Mr Alex Yam raised concern about section 32(d).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I wish to clarify that the amendments will specify the exact laws which can be overridden by directions issued under section 32(d).
